M2M Connectivity · WORKING GUIDE

Engineering proof readiness questions

One module can expose both connectivity layers; your logic defines routing, retry and priority.

Answer the engineering question inside A device, asset or worker reaches the edge of the cellular operating map and a missed message has an operational consequence.

Bring these inputs

  1. Operating regions and movement patterns
  2. Known or suspected coverage boundaries
  3. Message types, payload sizes and urgency
  4. Power, enclosure and antenna constraints
  5. Retry, acknowledgement and fallback behaviour
  6. Commercial outcome and decision timeline

This guide is a diagnostic starting point. It is not a coverage assessment, product certification or delivery guarantee.

Review the design questions

concepts.title: Coverage boundary
concepts.idea: Where does your device lose coverage?
concepts.audience: Product teams and system integrators whose connected devices move beyond dependable cellular coverage.
concepts.problem: Make the boundary visible: A device, asset or worker reaches the edge of the cellular operating map and a missed message has an operational consequence..
concepts.message: Coverage is a design question. Map where the preferred path stops, then plan what happens next.
concepts.supporting: Give Product teams and system integrators whose connected devices move beyond dependable cellular coverage. a simple way to see where Iridium Certus 9604 Hybrid IoT fits and what needs to be assessed in Australia + New Zealand.
concepts.why: This direction turns an abstract market problem into a recognisable moment that can earn attention quickly.
proofRequirements: A sourced description of the boundary or trigger
A clear definition of what the offer can and cannot do
risks: The hook becomes generic if the boundary is not concrete
The audience may not recognise the moment without a real example
concepts.route: Boundary signal → diagnostic guide → scoped assessment → qualified conversation
concepts.visual: A human or asset approaching a visible operating boundary; no embedded copy or invented customer proof.

concepts.title: Operational consequence
concepts.idea: What does one missed transmission cost?
concepts.audience: Product teams and system integrators whose connected devices move beyond dependable cellular coverage.
concepts.problem: Connect the trigger to the consequence: A device, asset or worker reaches the edge of the cellular operating map and a missed message has an operational consequence..
concepts.message: When a message matters, the cost of silence should be visible before the system is designed.
concepts.supporting: Show the operational decision behind Iridium Certus 9604 Hybrid IoT: what must travel, when it must travel and what a responsible fallback requires.
concepts.why: This direction makes the commercial value tangible by linking the problem to time, risk, cost or continuity.
proofRequirements: A credible use case or customer-safe scenario
Evidence that supports the proposed response
risks: The campaign needs a concrete consequence, not a fear statement
concepts.cta: Assess the cost of a missed message
concepts.route: Operational consequence → proof-led scenario → readiness offer → qualified conversation
concepts.visual: A field decision interrupted at the moment it matters; show consequence through context, not alarmist overlays.

concepts.title: Engineering proof
concepts.idea: One module. Both layers. Your logic.
concepts.audience: Product teams and system integrators whose connected devices move beyond dependable cellular coverage.
concepts.problem: Answer the engineering question inside A device, asset or worker reaches the edge of the cellular operating map and a missed message has an operational consequence..
concepts.message: One module can expose both connectivity layers; your logic defines routing, retry and priority.
concepts.supporting: Lead with the mechanism, the interfaces and the decisions that remain with the product team.
concepts.why: This direction earns trust with technically literate buyers who need proof and boundaries before a sales conversation.
proofRequirements: A qualified statement of what remains developer- or customer-defined
risks: A technical hook can lose non-engineering decision-makers
The mechanism must be explained without implying automatic outcomes
